question: Which organization provides coral bleaching alert services for Indian coral regions based on sea surface temperature data?

options.text: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (INCOIS)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)** is a specialized organization under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, Government of India, based in Hyderabad.
 
• INCOIS provides **coral bleaching alert services** based on **sea surface temperature (SST) data**. This service helps monitor and forecast bleaching events in coral regions, especially in Indian waters.
 
• Coral bleaching occurs due to prolonged exposure to **increased sea surface temperatures**, which stresses the corals and causes them to expel the symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) living within their tissues.
 
• The alert services provided by INCOIS are critical for **marine conservation** and **sustainable management of coral ecosystems**, which play a vital role in biodiversity and the livelihoods of coastal communities.
 
• INCOIS uses advanced ocean modeling tools, satellite data, and real-time analysis to predict and monitor changes in sea surface temperatures and their impact on coral reefs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS):**

 
 
• Established in **1999**, it operates under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana.
 
• INCOIS provides real-time ocean information and advisory services such as **tsunami warnings**, **fishing zone advisories**, and **marine weather forecasts**.
 
• It also collaborates with international organizations for the **Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS)** and regional initiatives to enhance its capabilities.
 
• Its research focuses on areas such as **climate change impacts, ocean circulation patterns**, and **marine biodiversity**.
 
 
 
• **Coral Bleaching:**
 
 
• Occurs when **sea surface temperatures** rise above the normal range, causing stress to corals and leading them to expel the **zooxanthellae algae**, which are responsible for their vibrant colors.
 
• Bleaching events can lead to **mass mortality** of coral reefs, impacting marine ecosystems and the livelihoods of communities dependent on them.
 
• Major bleaching events have occurred globally, such as the **2016 Great Barrier Reef bleaching**, caused by rising ocean temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Sea Surface Temperature (SST):**
 
 
• SST refers to the temperature of the ocean's surface layer, typically measured using **satellite data, buoys, and ship-based observations**.
 
• Changes in SST are indicators of ocean health and play a key role in **marine ecosystem dynamics** such as coral health, fish migration, and climate patterns.
 
 
 
• **Organizations related to marine conservation:**
 
 
• **Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI):** Focuses on **fisheries research** and conservation in India.
 
• **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI):** Conducts surveys of **faunal biodiversity**, including marine ecosystems.
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change:** Oversees policies on **environmental conservation**, including marine biodiversity protection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Coral Reefs:**

 
 
• Coral reefs are often referred to as the **"rainforests of the sea"** due to their rich biodiversity.
 
• They support **marine life**, act as natural barriers against coastal erosion, and contribute to **tourism and fisheries**.
 
 
 
• **Global Coral Bleaching Monitoring:**
 
 
• International organizations like NOAA (**National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration**) provide bleaching alerts globally.
 
• These systems use advanced satellite data and climate models to predict bleaching events.
